questions.question: Define plankton.Explain phytoplanktons and zooplanktons with examples.
questions.solution_html:
• • Plankton refers to the free-floating microorganisms. They must live in open water for at least
  • Anabaena. Zooplankton are animal-like planktons that depend on other organisms for food
  • protozoans, which feed on phytoplankton, bacteria and detritus. Eg: Amoeba, Paramecium.

questions.question: Describe the advantages and limitations of microbial biopesticides.
questions.solution_html:
• • Microbial biopesticides are microorganisms such as bacteria, fungi, viruses, or protozoa used
  • to control pests. Advantages: Environmentally Safe, Target Specificity, Safe to Humans and
  • Animals, Reduced Resistance Development, Eco-friendly Pest Management. Disadvantage
  • Slow Action, Narrow Spectrum, Environmental Sensitivity, Short Shelf Life.
questions.final_answer: Slow Action, Narrow Spectrum, Environmental Sensitivity, Short Shelf Life
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.solution_html:
• • Impaction methods are techniques used to collect airborne microorganisms by forcing air onto
  • a solid or semi-solid surface, where particles impact and get trapped.
  • Explain any two methods - Hollander and Dalla Valle Sampler, Slit sampler, Sieve Sampler.
questions.final_answer: Explain any two methods - Hollander and Dalla Valle Sampler, Slit sampler, Sieve Sampler

questions.question: / milk.
questions.solution_html:
• • The MPN method is a technique used to estimate the number of viable coliform bacteria in a
  • milk sample based on growth in liquid media. Coliforms ferment lactose and produce acid
  • and gas, which is used as an indicator. Explain the method briefly – Presumptive test
  • confirmatory test and completed test.
questions.final_answer: confirmatory test and completed test
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the different types of spoilage of milk.
questions.solution_html:
• • Milk is highly nutritious and easily spoiled by microorganisms. Spoilage results in undesirable
  • changes in taste, odour, texture, and appearance. Explain different spoilage in detail
  • Acidic Spoilage (Souring), Gas Production (Stormy Fermentation), Proteolytic Spoilage
  • (Putrefaction) , Ropiness Sliminess, Lipolytic Spoilage (Rancidity), Sweet Curdling - Caused by
  • spore-formers like Bacillus. Milk curdles without much acid production., Flavour changes
  • Discolorations etc.
questions.final_answer: Discolorations etc
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Explain the zonation of lakes with a neat labeled diagram and describe the microbial communities in lakes.

  • Explain each zone with a neat diagram - light compensation level, limnetic zone, littoral zone
  • Pelagic zone, euphotic zone, profundal zone, benthic zone. . Microbial Communities
questions.final_answer: Pelagic zone, euphotic zone, profundal zone, benthic zone. . Microbial Communities
